subject: Post-demo: reserved capacity SLO validation & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: reserved capacity SLO validation & next steps

Hi Elaine / Dave —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a proposed validation plan so we can align on acceptance criteria for dedicated capacity:

Key items we discussed (please correct anything I got wrong):
- Target SLAs: p95 latency target around 200–250ms for completed responses; p99 target TBD (we asked for clarity).
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline of ~150 concurrent end users with steady-state ~120 req/s, burst capacity up to ~400 concurrent users for short windows.
- Streaming: progressive token streaming is required for your UX — partial tokens should be delivered as they generate rather than a single final chunk.
- Payloads: typical response length ~300–450 tokens; some longer reports up to 2k tokens but those can be background jobs.

Next steps I propose (short list):
1) You share a representative prompt set + a small sample of non-sensitive queries (we only need text) so we can size throughput.
2) We run a two-stage validation:
   a) Lab runs in our sandbox on A100/H100 variants with synthetic concurrency traces to produce expected p50/p95/p99 numbers.
   b) A short reserved-capacity smoke test in your tenant (1–2 business days) under a controlled workload to validate end-to-end behavior (streaming, KV cache priming, autoscaling).
3) We provide a sizing recommendation (GPU type, instance counts, reserved throughput) and a short ops runbook that lists throttles, retries, and fallback policies.

I've attached our initial sizing proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf) which includes conservative throughput numbers for A100 vs H100. To make the lab runs useful, can you confirm:
- Your acceptable p95 and p99 targets for interactive flows?
- Expected average and 95th percentile response token counts?
- Any hard concurrency or burst windows tied to business events?

If that sounds right, I’ll spin up the lab runs and loop in our performance engineering lead (Lauren) to coordinate the test harness. Proposed test week: Nov 16–18 (tentative).

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side:

Acceptance targets (interactive dashboard flows):
- p95 latency target: <= 220ms for median-length responses (~350 tokens).
- p99 target: soft target <= 650ms; we recognize p99 will be harder for bursty scenarios.

Workload profile:
- Typical response: mean ~350 tokens; 90th pct ~900 tokens; long-form report (5% of traffic) up to ~2k tokens.
- Concurrency: steady ~150 concurrent users, average arrival rate ~120 req/s.
- Burst events: marketing promotions can spike concurrent users up to ~400 for ~15–45 minute windows.
- Streaming: yes — we need progressive partial tokens for prompt previews and low-latency UX.

Hardware preference / budget:
- Our engineers prefer H100 for headroom, but procurement is currently pushing for A100 (cost delta). We want sizing guidance for both options and a recommendation with cost/latency tradeoffs.

I’ve attached a CSV with recent traffic samples and token-length distributions (finex_perf_profile.csv). Sharing that should help with the lab sims.

We can do the test window Nov 16–18; pls coordinate with our infra team for IP allowlist and S3 access.

Elaine
Head of Product
Finex Analytics

Subject: Re: Post-demo: reserved capacity SLO validation & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the data, Elaine. Based on the sample and your targets, here’s a concrete two-stage validation plan and acceptance criteria. I’ll keep this high-level so you can share with procurement/infra: 

Stage 1 — Lab validation (no customer traffic)
- Goal: characterize p50/p95/p99 and throughput for A100 (8x80GB) and H100 (8x80GB) configurations with your token distribution.
- Workload: replay of provided CSV scaled to steady-state 120 req/s and a separate burst trace peaking at 400 concurrent connections for 30 minutes. Mix includes the 5% long-form flows.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (streaming and end-of-response), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate.
- Acceptance (lab): A configuration is viable if p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 700ms for interactive flows in steady-state. Streaming latency measured as time-to-first-byte should be <= 80ms p95.
- Outputs: recommended GPU count, expected reserved throughput (tokens/sec), and estimate of monthly cost delta between A100 and H100.

Stage 2 — Reserved-capacity smoke test (customer tenant)
- Goal: validate end-to-end streaming behavior, network egress, auth, and autoscale fallbacks with a small reserved pool for 24–48 hours.
- Workload: subset of production traffic or replay with identical distribution; we’ll coordinate a schedule and run several 30–60 minute burst tests.
- Acceptance (smoke): p95 <= 250ms and streaming TTFB <= 100ms for the majority of traffic (<5% errors). Any persistent p99 regressions or >2% error rate will be documented and cause a rollback.

Recommended initial configs to test in the lab: 
- A100 baseline: 4 x A100 80GB nodes (fp16, scheduler-optimized kernel), expected steady-state tokens/sec estimate: ~45k tokens/sec across cluster (conservative).
- H100 headroom: 3 x H100 80GB nodes (fp16 + tensor-optimizations), expected steady-state tokens/sec estimate: ~70k tokens/sec (better p95/p99).

Notes / knobs to validate during the runs:
- Batch sizing and dynamic batching window: tune to keep p95 in target while maximizing throughput.
- KV cache priming: for dialog flows we expect large cache hit improvements — we’ll run a priming pass to estimate benefit.
- Quantization: test fp16 and int8-ish profiles for the smaller model family (if you’re open to slightly lower quality for cost savings).

Action items for Finex:
- Grant S3 read access to samples (or upload to the drive link I shared).
- Provide a contact for allowlisting IPs (we’ll need an infra point-of-contact).
- Confirm whether we should exclude the 2k-token report flows from the interactive SLA (recommended).

I’ll create a short runbook and a Jira ticket for tracking. Proposed lab start: Nov 10 (internal) so we have results ahead of your Nov 16–18 smoke window. If that schedule works I’ll assign tasks and reserve compute.

Thanks — looping Lauren to book the lab runs.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
